tables.name: doctors
tables.description: Doctors on the clinic's staff roster.

columns.name: doctor_id
columns.doc: Unique doctor identifier.

columns.name: doctor_name
columns.doc: Doctor's name as shown on the roster.

columns.name: dept
columns.doc: Department code: 1 = general practice, 2 = paediatrics, 3 = cardiology, 4 = dermatology, 5 = orthopaedics.

columns.name: employed_since
columns.doc: Date the doctor joined the clinic staff, YYYY-MM-DD.

tables.name: patients
tables.description: People registered with the clinic as patients.

columns.name: patient_id
columns.doc: Unique patient identifier.

columns.name: patient_name
columns.doc: Patient's full name.

columns.name: birth_year
columns.doc: Four-digit year the patient was born.

columns.name: blood_type
columns.doc: Blood group recorded at registration, for example A+ or O-.

columns.name: registered_on
columns.doc: Date the patient first registered with the clinic, YYYY-MM-DD.

tables.name: appointments
tables.description: Consultations booked with the clinic's doctors.

columns.name: appt_id
columns.doc: Unique appointment identifier.

columns.name: patient_id
columns.doc: The patient who booked the appointment.

columns.name: doctor_id
columns.doc: The doctor the appointment is with.

columns.name: starts_at
columns.doc: Scheduled start in clinic local time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.

columns.name: slots
columns.doc: Number of 15-minute slots reserved for the appointment.

columns.name: status
columns.doc: Outcome code: 1 = attended, 2 = cancelled by the patient, 3 = patient did not show up, 4 = still booked.

columns.name: rx_id
columns.doc: Unique prescription identifier.

columns.name: appt_id
columns.doc: The appointment during which the drug was prescribed.

columns.name: drug
columns.doc: Name of the prescribed medication.

columns.name: course
columns.doc: Length of the treatment course in weeks.

tables.name: invoices
tables.description: Bills raised for appointments, including no-show and late-cancellation fees.

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.doc: Unique invoice identifier.

columns.name: appt_id
columns.doc: The appointment the invoice was raised for.

columns.name: amount
columns.doc: Total amount invoiced, in South African rand.

columns.name: issued_on
columns.doc: Invoice date, YYYY-MM-DD; the clinic's financial year runs from 1 March to the end of February and is named after the year in which it ends.

columns.name: payer
columns.doc: Billing party code: 1 = the patient directly, 2 = a private insurer, 3 = the patient's employer.

columns.name: state
columns.doc: Payment state code: 1 = unpaid, 2 = paid in full, 3 = part paid, 4 = written off.

questions.text: Which doctor has been on staff the longest?
questions.sql: SELECT doctor_name FROM doctors ORDER BY employed_since ASC LIMIT 1

questions.text: How many cardiologists do we employ?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM doctors WHERE dept = 3

questions.text: Count the appointments where the patient never turned up.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM appointments WHERE status = 3

needs_docs.fact: code 3 means the patient did not show up

questions.text: What is the longest consultation in the diary, in minutes?

needs_docs.fact: each slot is 15 minutes, so minutes = slots x 15

questions.text: Name the medicines that patients are put on for longer than 30 days.
questions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT drug FROM prescriptions WHERE course * 7 > 30 ORDER BY drug

needs_docs.fact: course length is measured in weeks, not days

questions.text: What have we invoiced in total, in rand?

needs_docs.fact: amounts are in South African rand

questions.text: How much did the clinic bill during the 2026 financial year?
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM invoices WHERE issued_on >= '2025-03-01' AND issued_on <= '2026-02-28'

needs_docs.fact: the 2026 financial year runs from 1 March 2025 to 28 February 2026

questions.text: Of all our invoices, how many go to a private insurer?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoices WHERE payer = 2

needs_docs.fact: code 2 means a private insurer is billed

questions.text: Invoices that are paid in full: how many are there?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoices WHERE state = 2
SELECT patient_name FROM patients WHERE birth_year < 1960 ORDER BY patient_name

readings.sql: SELECT d.doctor_name FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id GROUP BY d.doctor_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT d.doctor_name FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id GROUP BY d.doctor_id ORDER BY SUM(a.slots) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Diary fullness is counted as the number of appointments a doctor has.

ambiguous.text: Which medicine gets prescribed most often?

readings.sql: SELECT drug FROM prescriptions GROUP BY drug ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT p.drug FROM prescriptions p JOIN appointments a ON a.appt_id = p.appt_id GROUP BY p.drug ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT a.patient_id) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: A drug's popularity is counted in prescriptions written, however many patients they went to.

ambiguous.text: How much has Marcus Bell spent with us?

readings.sql: SELECT SUM(i.amount) FROM invoices i JOIN appointments a ON a.appt_id = i.appt_id JOIN patients p ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id WHERE p.patient_name = 'Marcus Bell'
SELECT SUM(i.amount) FROM invoices i JOIN appointments a ON a.appt_id = i.appt_id JOIN patients p ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id WHERE p.patient_name = 'Marcus Bell' AND i.state = 2

resolving_note.text: A patient's spend is the sum of every invoice raised for them, settled or not.

ambiguous.text: Who has the most recent appointment?

readings.gloss: latest start time, including future bookings
readings.sql: SELECT p.patient_name FROM appointments a JOIN patients p ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id ORDER BY a.starts_at DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT p.patient_name FROM appointments a JOIN patients p ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id WHERE a.status = 1 ORDER BY a.starts_at DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: The latest appointment is simply the one with the latest start time, even if it has not happened yet.

readings.sql: SELECT dept FROM doctors GROUP BY dept ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT d.dept FROM appointments a JOIN doctors d ON d.doctor_id = a.doctor_id GROUP BY d.dept ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Department size is measured by the number of doctors who work in it.
